deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a German prose page of history notes, probably lecture or school notes, on Alexander the Great's campaign against Persia. It continues directly from the previous page, which breaks off at 'Durch Verrätherei', and runs straight into the next page, which begins 'ihn zurück zu kehren'.

Content, step by step:
(1) Alexander takes Persepolis through treachery and seizes a treasure of 100,000 talents. He sets fire to the city and the palace.
(2) Meanwhile Darius has gathered troops (30,000 men).
(3) Alexander marches quickly to Media. Darius has already fled further east and put himself in the hands of Bessus, his satrap of Bactria. A first 'in die Hände' at the start of a line is struck through, because the phrase had already been written on the previous line.
(4) Bessus plans to found an independent kingdom in the East. Alexander passes through the Caspian Gates.
(5) When Bessus sees he cannot escape with the king, he deals Darius a fatal wound and crosses the Oxus.
(6) Alexander's men find the wounded king just as he dies. The left margin has the keyword 'Darius'.
(7) Alexander wants to punish Bessus, but a revolt in Aria forces him to turn back; the sentence continues on the next page.

There is no derivation, formula or calculation to reconstruct. The hand and the content (a historical narrative with schoolbook dates on adjacent pages) suggest pupil or lecture notes bound into the Nachlass. They may not be in Gauss's own hand, but that cannot be decided from this page alone.
errors: Not a mathematical error, a historical imprecision. Ancient sources (Diodorus, Curtius) give the Persepolis treasure as about 120,000 talents; Plutarch and Arrian give other or no figures. The page says 100,000.

Historical simplification: Darius was deposed and killed by a conspiracy of Bessus, Nabarzanes and Barsaentes. The page attributes the act to Bessus alone, which is a common schoolbook simplification.
Historical simplification: the tradition that Alexander's men found Darius still alive (the Polystratus story) is late and doubtful. Arrian says he was already dead when found.
